text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press at the weekend. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Sugar prices expected to rise at end-September.
- National Bank will launch new issue of Samurai bonds expected to rise some $300 million.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Energy stocks are insufficient for coming winter.
- Romania is confronted with energy shortage which diminishes its chances of integration into EU.
- Agriculture ministry to use 10,000 tonnes of edible oil from state reserves in order to avoid inevitable rise in oil prices, newspaper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Emil Constantinescu, opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) leader, slammed "Iliescu regime" for incompetent economic policy, increasing corruption and red tape.
- Constantinescu said Romania ranked among at the bottom of list of countries meeting requirements to join NATO and the European Union -- according to a German Bundesbank study.
- U.S. Ambassador to Bucharest Alfred Moses reportedly asked that Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) be included on U.S. government-funded aid programmes for emerging democracies.
- Five miners died in pit accident caused by explosion at Petrila coal mine in southwestern Romania.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Bucharest city hall issued decree to forbid selling of food produce on street stands to prevent spreading of viral meningitis epidemics which killed 28 people from a total of more than 400 people hospitalised with the disease.
- Full-page report on pop star Michael Jackson's arrival in Bucharest, as part of his tour to launch new album HIStory.
- Paliament commission allocated air time for each parliament party, to regulate parties' presence in state television and state radio programmes during election campaign.
- Ruling PDSR got weekly 83 minutes of air time on television, while opposition CDR and Democratic Party got 36 minutes each.
- Campaign on state TV and radio starts on September 16, and it starts on October 7 on local public stations.
ADEVARUL
- Romania could join EU as full member in 2002 and NATO in 2010, said Walter Althammer, head of Germany's Institute for southeast European Studies.

- Romanian presidency banned Emil Constantinescu from participating in ceremony of signing Romanian-Hungarian friendship treaty in Western city of Timisoara on Monday, saying political leaders, not presidential candidates have been invited.
- Social-Democratic Union -- of which former premier Petre Roman's PD is a member -- has joined Socialist International.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Restoration of Constantin Brancusi's Endless Column to start in south eastern town of Tirgu Jiu on Saturday.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- Police arrested two men for forging tourist visas for Italy.
ZIUA
- Viral meningitis epidemics is pretext for the opposition to demand that November 3 elections be postponed, PDSR statement said.
COTIDIANUL

- Mircea Carol, illegitimate son of Romania's pre-war King Carol II, has refused to attend his son's wedding to commoner Lia Triff, newspaper says quoting British daily Evening Standard. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
